scope: Read-only follow-up on explicit shared health, post-lock checks and waiter test.
closed_paths: Supervisor health is now an explicit required constructor parameter; no silent fresh health fallback.
Transition poisons before releasing the global lock after persistence failure; a waiting sibling rechecks health after acquiring the lock.
Snapshot/create/open also recheck health after lock acquisition and reject pre-poisoned constructors.
Frame/byte append limits poison the shared health.
The new named-channel waiter test specifically exercises a Transition Sync failure while B waits after its initial health check.

findings.location: server/internal/store/pilot_start_catalog.go: openPilotCatalogFromVerifiedHandle and Snapshot, known-error handling around Unlock
findings.detail: Both paths release the global lock before poisoning health for an already-known read/Sync/parent-Sync error. A sibling can acquire the released lock, pass its new post-lock health check and perform IO before the failing operation publishes poison. Transition is fixed, but these two equivalent release windows remain.
findings.required: Publish poison for an already-known operation error while still holding the global lock, then unlock. Continue classifying an Unlock error after it returns; do not postpone known-error publication until then.
findings.regression: Use an Unlock seam that releases the underlying gate and blocks before returning. Fail startup Sync or Snapshot read, let a sibling acquire during this window, and assert poisoned with zero sibling IO. This deterministically distinguishes poison-before-release from poison-after-release.

other_boundaries: No additional platform-lock finding in this follow-up; previous cross-process and bounded-supervision acceptance limitations remain.
Waiter test channels currently rely on the enclosing test process timeout for failure cleanup; bounded waits and joining workers before TempDir cleanup are recommended before wider fault execution.
execution: No tests, builds, services or code modifications.
